what_this_is: A searchable index of the curves, methods, factor bases, candidate identities, tournament rounds and ecbench sessions this repository names, joined on the identities it already computes (ICV1 slugs, EC1 aliases, ECM1 method ids, FB1 factor-base ids, IC1 candidate ids). Every figure is quoted from a committed file named in `sources` or in the row; nothing is computed here beyond means over a session's own verified runs.

oracles.name: subtract
oracles.what: Decompose a point by subtracting factor-base points directly; no table.

oracles.name: mitm
oracles.what: Meet-in-the-middle over pair sums of the base; `m=2|3`; `negation_folded=1` halves the table under the negation map (prime and binary bases).

oracles.name: mitm-frobenius
oracles.what: Meet-in-the-middle with the table folded under Frobenius; needs a Frobenius-closed base (Koblitz orbit bases).

oracles.name: descent-algebraic
oracles.what: Summation-polynomial decomposition solved algebraically; needs `--solver`. Nondeterministic under a solver budget, so excluded from cross-method ecbench baselines.

oracles.name: matrix-f4
oracles.what: Boolean Macaulay matrices to a fixed degree, propagation and splitting (koblitz_groebner MatrixF4).

oracles.name: pair_table / pair_or_triple
oracles.what: Pair (or pair-then-triple) sum table decomposition in the tournament's native solver; the incumbent's oracle.

oracles.name: semaev_s3_roots, semaev_s4_pairs_and_solve
oracles.what: Third and fourth summation polynomials solved by root finding; historical ladder variants.

solvers.name: buchberger-f2
solvers.what: Gröbner basis over F2 by Buchberger's algorithm.

solvers.name: fes-f2, fes-f2-wide
solvers.what: Fast exhaustive search over F2, Gray-code enumeration.

solvers.name: crossbred-f2
solvers.what: Crossbred: partial linearisation then exhaustive search.

solvers.name: sat-cdcl
solvers.what: Native CDCL SAT with XOR reasoning on the Boolean encoding.

solvers.name: exhaustive
solvers.what: Plain enumeration; the reference for correctness.

solvers.name: wdsat, cryptominisat, magma-f4
solvers.what: External solvers named in the SAT factor-base review; historical, not in the native pipeline.

factor_base_families.name: prime-abscissa
factor_base_families.what: The points whose abscissa is below a bound on a prime-field curve.

factor_base_families.name: koblitz-orbit
factor_base_families.what: A Frobenius-invariant subspace of abscissae named by factors of x^n - 1; Frobenius-closed, so the table folds.

factor_base_families.name: binary-subspace
factor_base_families.what: Abscissae in a polynomial-basis F2-subspace; needs no invariant factor, so not Frobenius-closed.

factor_base_families.name: compact-orbit-scan
factor_base_families.what: Orbit base built by scanning a compact representative set.

factor_base_families.name: glv-orbit
factor_base_families.what: Orbit base under a GLV endomorphism on a prime-field curve.

factor_base_families.name: gls-line
factor_base_families.what: Line base under a GLS endomorphism on an extension-field curve.

factor_base_families.name: symmetrised / koblitz-symmetrised
factor_base_families.what: Bases closed under negation and Frobenius so that one column stands for an orbit.

A column is the orbit representative itself rather than [h] of it. The representative is already in the order-r subgroup -- it is a Frobenius image of a point the sampler projected with [h] -- so the second cofactor multiplication scaled every column by a constant and the row and the descent carried a matching constant to compensate. Dropping all four leaves the same logarithms and saves K scalar multiplications by the cofactor per job, which is most of the base phase wherever h is large (12,646 at n29a1; 1,492 at n31a0). The report declares column_convention: representative and the checker, amended additively by round18-oracle-convention.patch, verifies under either convention.

Both patches. The levers are disjoint -- one is the setup's cofactor multiplications, the other the collection's scan block -- so their instruction gains should compose almost exactly. Development measures 0.9621 panel-wide against the incumbent, against 0.9867 for block alone and 0.9757 for column alone.

The rule's shape is unchanged and so is every cell whose own value is already at or below 16 -- n13a0, n17a1, n19a0 and n29a1, which therefore act as an A/A control carried inside a live arm. Measured over the round-0017 panel, the rule asks for a block past its own optimum wherever it exceeds 16: at n23a1 it asks for 102, which costs 1.040x what 16 costs. Predictions are in ROUND18-single-target.md.

A column is the orbit representative itself rather than [h] of it. The representative is already in the order-r subgroup -- it is a Frobenius image of a point the sampler projected with [h] -- so the second cofactor multiplication scaled every column by a constant and the row and the descent carried a matching constant to compensate. Dropping all four leaves the same logarithms and saves K scalar multiplications by the cofactor per job, which is most of the base phase wherever h is large (12,646 at n29a1; 1,492 at n31a0). The report declares column_convention: representative and the checker, amended additively by round18-oracle-convention.patch, verifies under either convention.

Both patches. The levers are disjoint -- one is the setup's cofactor multiplications, the other the collection's scan block -- so their instruction gains should compose almost exactly. Development measures 0.9621 panel-wide against the incumbent, against 0.9867 for block alone and 0.9757 for column alone.

Round 0018's two levers together, unchanged: round18-block.patch lowers the scan block's clamp ceiling from 64 to 16, and round18-column.patch makes a column the orbit representative itself rather than [h] of it, dropping the matching factor of h from the row and the descent and declaring column_convention: representative. Round 0018b measured it at 0.9652 [0.9448, 0.9828] against the incumbent in instructions and 0.9613 [0.9288, 0.9895] natively, passing the no-regression gate on both final stages and failing only the strict rho gate, at n23a1 alone. Round 0019 re-runs it under a fresh seed with forty confirmation fixtures at that cell instead of twelve, which is the number ROUND19-single-target.md sec. 5 derives from the cell's own frozen spread. No new lever: sec. 3's base-size model says the contract's factor base is already at its optimum at n23a1 and the curve around it is flat.

candidates.hypothesis: The same incumbent rounds 0017, 0018b and 0019 all measured, worker sha256 e9f263b8. It stays the baseline rather than being replaced by round 0019's promoted winner, because a replication must re-measure the same comparison: promoting `both` into the baseline would make both/incumbent identically 1 and destroy the quantity under test.

Round 0018's two levers together, byte-identical to the arm round 0019 promoted. Round 0019 measured it at 0.6751 [0.6298, 0.7265] against rho in instructions and 0.8848 [0.8624, 0.9098] natively, below one at every cell in both metrics on both final stages, with n23a1 at 0.7498 on forty fixtures. Round 0020 changes the seed and nothing else. Predictions are in ROUND20-single-target.md.

The round-0020 winner, widened so it can run above degree 31, with max_trials raised 4096 -> 65536 so rho completes at every cell. Round 0021 measured the widening at 1.0007x the promoted worker with identical logarithms and factor bases on all eight panel cells; round 0022 bounded the cap change at 14 ppm on either arm. Its factor base is the case's: points = 6*degree, one batch of eight orbits at every cell.

The orbit count follows the subgroup order: 8*round((r/4196903)^0.157), never fewer than one batch. That is exactly one batch on all eight panel cells, so the arm should be the incumbent there to within the literal it parses, and 16 at n37a0 and 24 at n43a1, n59a0 and n61a1. The rule is fitted to round 0022's measured optima at n23a1, n37a0 and n43a1; n59a0 and n61a1 are outside the range it was fitted on and enter as holdouts.
